entities.summary: Belarus is a sovereign nation in Eastern Europe, Europe. Its capital is Minsk. Official languages include Belarusian, Russian. Government: Unitary presidential republic (authoritarian). Population: approximately 9.2 million. Area: 207,600 km². Comprehensive index for Belarus covering Slavic settlement, Kievan Rus, Grand Duchy of Lithuania (major component, Belarusian = GDL literary language), Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Russian Empire (partitions of Poland), WWI/WWII devastation (25% population killed WWII, Brest-Litovsk Treaty 1918), Byelorussian SSR (founding USSR member 1922), Chernobyl disaster 1986 (70% fallout on Belarus), independence 1991, Lukashenko dictatorship (1994-present, 'Europe's last dictator'), 2020 protests (Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya), and Russia alliance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Belarus's experience under Soviet rule and its subsequent independence have had a significant regional impact, with the country playing a key role in Eastern European politics. The 2020 protests, led by Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, highlighted the nation's struggle for democratic reform.
